title: The Codex sandbox blocks the network. It can still read the key.
friendlyTitle: Codex can be boxed in. It can still read a key.
summary: On 18 November, OpenAI described the default Codex sandbox for a Git project. Commands may write in the workspace, while .git and .codex stay read-only, and network access is off. Reads are broad, limited by the operating system's own permissions.
friendlySummary: On 18 November, OpenAI described the default box around Codex in a Git project. It may change files in the project. The Git folder and the Codex settings stay read-only. The network is off. It can still read many other files, if your computer already allows that.
whyItMatters: OpenAI says a command may still read a config file that holds an API key, and that a change in an ignored folder can later run outside the sandbox. The fence is the permission profile you set. A blocked upload is not the same as a hidden secret.
friendlyWhyItMatters: OpenAI says a command may still read a settings file that holds an API key. A change in a folder Git ignores can later run outside the box. You set the limits. Blocking an upload does not hide a secret.
